title: Beyond executive dysfunction: The precuneus as an introspective monitoring hub for driving safety
title_zh: 超越执行功能障碍：顶后叶作为驾驶安全的内省监测枢纽
abstract: Unsafe driving is a public health concern, yet its neural basis in the general population remains poorly understood. Research on attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) traditionally attributes crash risk to executive dysfunction and fronto-striatal abnormalities, but these models do not explain unsafe driving among healthy individuals. Here, we synthesize structural and functional neuroimaging evidence to propose a precuneus-centered framework of driving safety. Reduced precuneus gray matter volume is associated with ADHD trait dimensions and crash history in healthy adults, while functional neuroimaging indicates precuneus involvement during driving-related hazard appraisal. Together, these findings suggest that crash vulnerability may be associated with impaired metacognitive awareness of internal states rather than primary executive deficits. The framework proposes that introspective monitoring may facilitate subsequent executive regulation, while recognizing that this temporal ordering remains a conceptual hypothesis. By conceptualizing the precuneus as an introspective monitoring hub within a broader distributed neurocognitive network, this framework links default mode network research with safety-critical behavior and offers a neurobiological perspective on driving risk.
abstract_zh: 不安全驾驶是公共卫生关注点，但其在普通人群中的神经基础尚不清楚。关于注意缺陷多动障碍（ADHD）的研究传统上将事故风险归因于执行功能障碍和额纹状体异常，但这些模型无法解释健康个体的不安全驾驶。本文综合结构和功能神经影像证据，提出以顶后叶为中心的驾驶安全框架。顶后叶灰质体积减少与ADHD特质维度及健康成年人事故史相关，而功能影像显示顶后叶在驾驶相关危险评估中发挥作用。综合这些发现，提示事故易感性可能与内部状态的元认知意识受损有关，而非主要的执行功能缺陷。该框架提出内省监测可能促进随后的执行调节，尽管这种时间顺序仍是概念假设。通过将顶后叶视为更广泛分布式神经认知网络中的内省监测枢纽，该框架将默认模式网络研究与安全关键行为联系起来，并提供了驾驶风险的神经生物学视角。
